title: Phase 1.5 De-Async Repair Sweep
description:
Phase 1.5 of the Interactive Job Runtime Refactor (master ticket 26/08/20/INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR). Unplanned but prerequisite.

A full cargo check --workspace --all-targets reports ~676 in-scope errors. Attribution verified, not assumed: semio-framework-ui (557 under feature unification, mainly the wgpu-engine feature), semio-framework-2d (28), semio-framework-graph (8), semio-framework-machine-derive (4), semio-s-plugin-draw-fsm (5), semio-framework-ui-backend-vulkan (1) are all UNMODIFIED in the working tree, and there are zero commits since the baseline commit, so their content is baseline content. The repo did not build before this refactor began. semio-hub (31 + 39) was touched by Phase 1 and needs separate attribution. semio-compose-rs is out of scope.

Every error is one bug class: async fn called without .await. Signatures include "no method named X found for opaque type impl Future", "cannot apply unary operator ! to type impl Future<Output = bool>", "the ? operator can only be applied to values that implement Try", "impl Future<Output = Vec<..>> is not an iterator", and "cannot subtract impl Future from impl Future". This is the mechanical fallout of the repo-wide async convention recorded at AGENTS.md line 44. Phase 0's census measured the same phenomenon from the other side: 88.28% of 53,338 async fn are effectively non-suspending.

Why this must happen now: Phases 3 and 5 rewrite the UI runtime and convert the run-to-completion frame transaction into a resumable worker-owned state machine. They cannot land on crates that do not compile under the workspace feature set, and semio-framework-ui's wgpu-engine feature is precisely the code they target.

Approach: repair with compiler-verified, span-keyed edits driven by Phase 0's 🔧️async-census.json. Never name-keyed edits, which silently hit unrelated production code. For each broken call site decide deliberately between awaiting a genuinely suspending callee and removing async from a callee that never suspends; prefer removing async where the function has no suspension point, since that is the refactor's direction of travel.

Already fixed as an unblocker: ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🧩️puzzle/📦️packages/🦀️rust/build.rs had an illegal async fn main() plus an async fn out_dir() called without .await, so it had never compiled.

Exit gate: cargo check --workspace --all-targets is clean for all in-scope crates, with compose excluded; no new third-party dependencies; the async census is re-run so the recorded A/B/C/D split reflects the repaired tree.
